title: Listening as a Lost Skill
sentences: Music has become almost impossible to avoid and correspondingly easy to ignore entirely.
It now accompanies shopping, waiting, exercising and a considerable amount of ordinary daily work.
In each of those cases it is doing something other than being actually listened to.
Attention given to a piece from beginning to end has become faintly unusual behaviour.
The recording industry did not conspire at any point to bring this about.
It simply became far cheaper to have music everywhere than to have it anywhere in particular.
Abundance has a reliable way of converting an occasion into a permanent background texture.
The loss is unusually difficult to articulate precisely because nothing at all was ever taken away.
Everything remains permanently available to us, which is exactly the mechanism at work.
What has become scarce is not the music itself but the silence that framed it.
